nytimes_articles.abstract: Federal Judge Scott Wright rules that proposed merger between Utilicorp United Inc and Kansas City Power and Light Co is subject to Missouri law requiring two-thirds vote of shareholders for approval; two companies had argued that Missouri law is not applicable and that only simple majority of shareholders is needed to approve merger (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: France Gives Details Of Thomson Sale
nytimes_articles.abstract: French Government says privatization of Thomson SA, a military contractor, will be through direct sale to investors and reaffirms that sale will be before end of 1996; Government says it will retain a share (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Letter from Daniel Olden on removal of old arrivals-and-departures board in Grand Central Terminal; drawing (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Peter Froman letter says it is not surprising that New York City transit metro card has not caught on when it is of such limited use

nytimes_articles.headline: Dollar Falls After Jobs Report Suggests No Rise in U.S. Rates
nytimes_articles.abstract: US dollar ends slightly lower after July employment report bolsters expectations that US interest rates would remain steady (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Eurocopter Sells Saudis 12 Helicopters
nytimes_articles.abstract: Saudi Arabia agrees to buy 12 search-and-rescue helicopters made by French-German venture Eurocopter; contract's value is not given (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Export Growth Slows for Asia's Tiger Economies
nytimes_articles.abstract: Export growth for many countries in East Asian region--including original 'Four Tigers' of Singapore, Taiwan, Hong Kong and South Korea, as well as half-dozen other countries that are following the same fast-growth path--has slowed sharply this year; and China's exports have actually declined; deceleration in part reflects healthy cooling off of economies that were running risk of overheating; but it also raises questions about staying power of East Asia's export-driven economic boom; in particular, it translates into deterioration of region's trade balance; that, in turn, threatens to drag area's currencies lower against the dollar and the yen, a development that could lead to unpredictable economic consequences; graph (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: U.S. and Japan Renew a Chip Accord, but With Changes
nytimes_articles.abstract: US and Japan agree to new and unusual trade accord governing computer chip industry, one that reflects the revival of American electronics industry since first accord was signed a decade ago; agreement will allow Pres Clinton when he visits Silicon Valley next week to assert that he has pressed Japan into an agreement that keeps up the pressure for continued American expansion in the market that strikes at the heart of Japan's greatest technological strength; Japanese Government, which wanted to kill off chip agreement, signs new, three-year agreement only after US accedes to Japan's demand that two Governments get out of business of measuring the share of Japan's market that foreign companies have secured (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Different Verdict in Little Rock
nytimes_articles.abstract: Editorial says acquittal in latest Whitewater case leaves conspiracy itself unproved, but Kenneth Starr, court-appointed independent counsel, still has much work to do; says he is moving properly to fulfill heart of his mission, but he must be doubly careful in election year not to appear to be playing political games (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Power Through Cyberspace
nytimes_articles.abstract: There is burgeoning movement, from Harlem to the South Bronx, to carry the Internet to children of poorer neighborhoods; from library computer lab in Flatbush, Bklyn, to Internet cafe in East Harlem to projects giving free public access to World Wide Web, organizations, educators and entrepreneurs have new message for the poor: there is power in cyberspace; photos (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: With a Stable Economy, Clinton Hopes for Credit
nytimes_articles.abstract: Last article in The Clinton Record series discusses the President's economic successes and failures of the past four years as Clinton focuses his re-election campaign on a substantially improved economy and tries to convince middle-class voters that he has not forgotten them; excerpts from Clinton interview; charts; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Gant Slam Ruins Night For Jones And Mets
nytimes_articles.abstract: St Louis Cardinals defeat New York Mets, 4-3; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Cram Course in Priorities: Food and Sex
nytimes_articles.abstract: Teenage Romeo and pal scheme to sell cheap sunglasses. Contrived, simple-minded comedy.

nytimes_articles.abstract: D Wayne Lukas is in town to prepare his horses for running of Whitney Handicap and Jim Dandy Stakes at Saratoga Springs, NY, and Haskell Invitational at Monmouth Race Track in Oceanport, NJ (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Corrections
Mexican Whistle-Blower Held on Drug Charge
nytimes_articles.abstract: Ricardo Cordero Ontiveros, former official of Mexican anti-drug unit who accused former colleagues of narcotics trafficking and bribery, is himself arrested on same charges; spokesman for Mexico's Attorney General denies that timing of Cordero's arrest was related to his public accusations against others; Cordero's wife maintains that Government trumped up charges against her husband in reprisal for his whistle-blowing crusade (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Official Asks If President Of Adelphi Should Stay
nytimes_articles.abstract: Adelphi University's enrollment is dropping sharply, its money is limited and its campus is in turmoil; New York State Board of Regents president J Edward Meyer asks Adelphi's president Peter Diamandopoulos whether he can effectively continue in office; Regeents Board is holding hearings in Manhattan on petition to remove Adelphi's board; Diamandopoulos agrees that controversies surrounding him must be resolved for Adelphi to move forward, but he says he does not intend to quit (L)6

nytimes_articles.headline: Evidence Was Just Enough
nytimes_articles.abstract: Sean Washington and Kevin Baker are convicted in murders of Margaret Wilson and Rodney Turner in January 1995 in Camden, NJ (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Five U.S. Boats Again Fail to Advance
nytimes_articles.abstract: US sends five boats into canoe-kayak semifinals at Olympic Games, and all five fail to advance; Italy sends five boats to flatwater events and each will race in the finals (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Dwindling Down to a Precious Few
nytimes_articles.abstract: Roundup of highlights of Olympic events on Day 15; table of medal leaders

nytimes_articles.headline: Discounts in Chicago
nytimes_articles.abstract: Randolph C Hauer letter suggests New York City transit system adopt Chicago's discount-fare policies

nytimes_articles.headline: Serb Fighter Now Fights Ruling Party In Bosnia
nytimes_articles.abstract: Milovan Stankovic, former officer in Bosnian Serb army, has started newspaper that opposes leadership in Serb-controlled Bosnia; he has attacked politicians, and even the army that led Bosnia's Serbs into what he calls isolation and disaster; he claims hard-line politicians turned out to be war profiteers, and the army he helped lead was in fact an armed gang; Stankovic wants to help mold new government, and he is using his standing as authority to criticize, something many Bosnian Serbs are afraid to do; photo; map (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Rival to Perot Picks His Running Mate
nytimes_articles.abstract: Richard D Lamm, who is seeking Reform Party's nomination as its Presidential candidate, says he chose former Rep Ed Zschau as his running mate (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Dole Asserts Clinton Violated Election Law
nytimes_articles.abstract: Dole campaign says Clinton White House illegally used taxpayer money for partisan political purposes; Dole forces send letter to Federal Election Commission, saying that White House used staff and resources to create shadow campaign organization (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: New Nassau County Legislature Draws Crowds and Critics
nytimes_articles.abstract: Newly created Nassau County Legislature, under Board of Supervisors it replaced, regularly draws overflow crowds to its chamber in Mineola, LI; after seven months there is growing debate over the Legislature; defenders say it is making a difference, but critics see it as a reincarnation of old Nassau and its vaunted Republican Party; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: An Exuberant Portrayer Of Beckettian Distress
nytimes_articles.abstract: Rosaleen Linehan, Ireland's favorite actress, discusses difficulties of her role in Samuel Beckett's play Happy Days, presented during Lincoln Center Festival '96; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Bankers' Jurors Disbelieved Chief Prosecution Witness
nytimes_articles.abstract: Jurors in latest case brought by Whitewater independent counsel's office say they voted to acquit two Arkansas bankers of four felony counts because Neal T Ainley, Government's main witness, appeared evasive during his testimony; Ainley, former bank president, accused defendants, bank's owners, of instructing him to conceal from Government large cash withdrawals made by Bill Clinton's 1990 campaign for governor; most jurors find videotaped testimony of Pres Clinton to be irrelevant to their deliberations; jurors say that even after they reached a decision, there remained some disagreement among them about what had occurred (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Key Rates
In Shift, Islam Is Unaffected by 2 Deadly Incidents
nytimes_articles.abstract: American Muslim organizations say relatively little suspicion or hostility was directed toward broad Muslim community after crash of TWA Flight 800 and lethal bomb blast at the Olympics in Atlanta, Ga; that was not the case in immediate aftermath of Oklahoma City bombing in April 1995, when television reports speculated that the attack was work of Middle East terrorists (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Returnees Ante Up Venture Capital: Their Ideas
nytimes_articles.abstract: Hundreds of young Vietnamese-born Americans have returned to Vietnam in the last few years to do business and to seek their roots; many express uncertainty over their cultural identities, and Vietnamese Government seems equally divided between wanting the money and expertise they bring back and fearing Western cultural influences; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: No Pause to Refresh
nytimes_articles.abstract: Letter from Robert Solomon on confusing signs in New York City (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Fare-Increase Ploy?
nytimes_articles.abstract: Robert Johnson letter suspects New York City transit metrocard is part of scheme to raise fares

nytimes_articles.headline: North Korea to Open Its Airspace to Others
nytimes_articles.abstract: North Korea will allow overflight by international airlines, including carriers based in South Korea; agreement comes after 16 months of negotiations; it could save airlines more than $125 million a year in fuel costs; move appears to be part of cautious opening by North Korea (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Harness Drivers Free From Major Charges
nytimes_articles.abstract: Grand larceny charges against Herve Filion, harness racing's top driver, and Darron Ryder, Frederick Grant, David Ingraham and Daniel Kramer are dismissed by Westchester County Judge Kenneth Lange who says allegations do not fit the charge; five men, accused of elaborate scheme to fix races at Yonkers Raceway, still face lesser charges of conspiracy and sports tampering (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: 2d Nicotine Patch to Be Sold Over Counter
nytimes_articles.abstract: Food and Drug Administration approves second nicotine patch, Nicoderm CQ, for sale without prescription; Nicoderm will come in three strengths, so smokers can gradually wean themselves off cigarettes; studies show Nicoderm helps about 20 percent of smokers to quit, at least temporarily; that is about same success rate as achieved by other anti-smoking aids (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: NEWS SUMMARY
Judge Imposes a Big Payment on Ford
nytimes_articles.abstract: Ford Motor Co has been ordered to pay $10 million to plaintiffs in lawsuit for what Texas State District Judge Candace Tyson calls 'wrongful and abusive conduct' by Ford during pretrial proceedings; family and survivors of Heather Cohen, who died in 1991 accident involving Ford Probe, sued company, contending that her car's brakes had had a 'catastrophic failure'; Ford then sued parents of Cohen's daughter, 'seeking to get money back from them for damages they would receive from the accident' (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Taylor to Give Drug Talks
nytimes_articles.abstract: Former New York Giants linebacker Lawrence Taylor will warn high school football players about dangers of drugs as part of out-of-court settlement of charge of trying to buy crack cocaine; Tommy Brittain, Taylor's lawyer, says his client must perform 60 hours of community service, get drug counseling and undergo random drug testing under agreement with prosecutors (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Edmund Fogarty, 76, Priest Who Headed Child Care Services
nytimes_articles.abstract: Msgr Edmund F Fogarty, child care specialist who spent two decades with Catholic Charities of Archdiocese of New York, dies at age of 76 (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Carjackings Up; Gangs Cited
nytimes_articles.abstract: New Jersey State Police say reports of carjacking and domestic violence increased dramatically in the state during 1995; state police spokesman John Hagerty says there were 781 carjackings reported last year, compared with 574 the year before, perhaps because crime has become initiation rite for would-be gang members; incidents of domestic violence climbed to 86,621 last year from 70,991 in 1994 (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Michael M. Rea, 69, A Collector of Art And First Editions
nytimes_articles.abstract: Michael M Rea, art collector and publisher who established Rea Award for the Short Story, dies at age of 69 (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: BUSINESS DIGEST
Chicago Protesters Get Time Slots
nytimes_articles.abstract: Spots for protesters at Democratic National Convention in Chicago are being determined by lottery; it is part of city's effort to keep tight control of demonstrations at convention to avoid repeat of 1968, last time Democrats met in Chicago, when city police and anti-war demonstrators clashed for four bloody days and nights; Mayor Richard M Daley is determined not to suffer same embarrassments as his father, Mayor Richard J Daley, did when tear gas and rage shrouded city and stained Chicago and reputation of its Police Department; several lawsuits have been filed in Federal court challenging city's plans as abridgment of free speech; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Brands's Intensity Salvages Day for U.S.
nytimes_articles.abstract: Tom Brands of US wins gold medal in freestyle wrestling at 136.5 pounds at Olympic Games; he defeats South Korea's Jang Jae Sung in the final; Bruce Baumgartner of US wins bronze medal in superheavyweight (286-pound) class in judge's decision over Andrei Shumilin of Russia; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Kiptanui's Long Wait Becomes 4 Years Longer
nytimes_articles.abstract: Joseph Keter of Kenya wins gold medal in steeplechase event at Olympic Games with time of 8 minutes, 7.12 seconds, with fellow Kenyan Moses Kiptanui coming in second in 8:08.33; Alessandro Lambruschini of Italy claims the bronze with time of 8:11.28; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Visitors to Check for Fraud
nytimes_articles.abstract: New Jersey officials will hire private firm to help municipalities expose welfare recipients who use false address to collect benefits from more than one source; officials are hoping to cut down on estimated $3.2 million in welfare fraud (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Don't Stop Recycling

nytimes_articles.headline: Ex-Copper Trader Is Sentenced in Chile
nytimes_articles.abstract: Chilean Judge Jose Benquis sentences Juan Pablo Davila, former copper trader, to three years in prison for tax evasion in first conviction from 1994 futures trading scandal that cost Chile $175 million; Benquis also fines Davila 133 million pesos ($324 million) (S)p

nytimes_articles.headline: All in the Wrist?
nytimes_articles.abstract: Mort Gordon letter on intricacy of using New York City transit metrocard

nytimes_articles.headline: Agency Proposes Cut in Lilco Rates
nytimes_articles.abstract: Staff of State Public Service Commission, citing 'poor economic conditions on Long Island' linked to high electric costs, proposes 5.2 percent reduction in rates of Long Island Lighting Co; Lilco immediately objects, saying reduction would jeopardize service and reliability for its more than one million customers by cutting its operating and maintenance budget by $55.7 million a year (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: ISRAEL WILL ALLOW SETTLERS TO BUILD
nytimes_articles.abstract: Government of Prime Min Benjamin Netanyahu takes one of its first specific steps toward reversing the dovish policies of its predecessors, lifting Israel's four-year-old freeze on the expansion of settlements in the West Bank and Gaza; maps (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: New Jobs Data Brighten Mood On Wall Street
nytimes_articles.abstract: Negative mood of nation's financial markets evaporates after July employment report signals that economy might be slowing down a little; yield on 30-year bond drops to 6.73 percent from 6.83 percent, while Dow Jones industrial average climbs 85.08 points, or 1.5 percent, to 5,679.83; chart (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Drama at Track, and Upset on Tennis Court
nytimes_articles.abstract: Jackie Joyner-Kersee ends her Olympic career with bronze medal in the long jump, while Chioma Ajunwa of Nigeria takes the gold and sets an African record; in tennis, Lindsay Davenport of the United States takes the gold, beating Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain in women's singles; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Casinos Rake In Less
nytimes_articles.abstract: Figures released by Casino Association of New Jersey show gambling industry's winning streak abated somewhat last month, with casino revenues in Atlantic City, NJ, showing 1.4 percent decrease, to $363.1 million, from $368.4 million, compared with July 1995 (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Newman Seems to Be the Target
nytimes_articles.abstract: New York Athletic Commission is standing firm one day after it announced that it is temporarily suspending licenses of Lou Duva and Rock Newman's Spencer Promotions and withholding $1 million of Riddick Bowe's $5 million purse in aftermath of July 11 brawl at Madison Square Garden after Bowe's heavyweight bout with Andrew Golota (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Americans' Final Hurdle Is Brazil
nytimes_articles.abstract: US women's basketball team defeats team from Australia, 93-71, at Olympic Games to earn spot in championship game on Aug 4 against team from Brazil; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Myanmar Sanctions
nytimes_articles.abstract: Letter by New York City Councilman Thomas K Duane notes bill to deny city contracts to corporations that do business with Government in Myanmar (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: GERBER SCIENTIFIC APPOINTS ACTING CHIEF
nytimes_articles.abstract: Gerber Scientific Inc says its board appointed George Gentile as president, acting chief executive officer and chief operating officer because of continuing illness of Joseph Gerber, its chairman and chief executive officer (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Raise Your Hand if You Love Metrocard
nytimes_articles.abstract: Eric L Lazar letter on shortcomings of New York City transit metrocard

nytimes_articles.headline: Airline Settles Suit Over False Accusation
nytimes_articles.abstract: British Airways settles defamation lawsuit with Gillian MacIntosh Hernandez of New York City who had sued airline for accusing her of abandoning a newborn at Heathrow Airport in London in February; Hernandez's lawyer says airline employees had overlooked that Hernandez is black and that baby boy found in trash can in a bathroom was white; amount of settlment is not disclosed; Hernandez filed $10 million defamation suit in Federal District Court in Manhattan against British Airways on Aug 1; she and a friend each sought $5 million for emotion distress and slander (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Judicial Activism Of a Different Flavor
nytimes_articles.abstract: Andrew Dwyer letter charges Judge Jackson L Kiser is coddling criminals and legislating from the bench in invalidating Violence Against Women Act (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Russia's Dmitri Sautin captures gold medal in 10-meter platform diving event at Olympic Games; Germany's Jan Hempel wins the silver and China's Xiao Hailiang takes the bronze; Americans end up winning no golds in diving events, and last time that happened in an Olympics in which Americans competed was 1912 in Stockholm, Sweden (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Harbaugh Takes 4-Year Deal
nytimes_articles.abstract: Indianapolis Colts' backup quarterback Jim Harbaugh signs four-year contract with the team worth $13 million, including $4 million signing bonus (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Rodman Will Return to Bulls
nytimes_articles.abstract: Dennis Rodman has decided to return to Chicago Bulls next season; Rodman agrees to one-year contract, valued at between $6 million and $10 million (S)ï

nytimes_articles.headline: Putting a Number to the Monthly Gyration in Bonds
nytimes_articles.abstract: Study by Princeton University labor economist Alan B Krueger has found remarkably consistent correlation between interest rate on 30-year Treasury bond and job creation; more specifically, Krueger formula focuses on spread between what Wall Street's forecasters say the new jobs number will be, and what number actually is in Labor Department's announcement on first Friday morning of each month (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Clinton Campaign Joins Effort For Free Time on Television
nytimes_articles.abstract: Clinton campaign announces that it would help create system of free, uniform blocks of television time for Presidential candidates this fall, adding its weight to Dole campaign's and increasing pressure on networks to provide the time; Sens John McCain, Republican, and Bill Bradley, Democrat, both support Free TV for Straight Talk Coalition; they invite heads of cable and broadcast networks to meet with Presidential campaigns before September; several networks have already offered free air time in varying formats this fall, but coalition is hoping to create uniform system that would serve as model for future races (M)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Photo of Omar Linares and Luis Ulacia of Cuba, which takes the Olympic gold medal in baseball in 13-9 victory overy Japan

nytimes_articles.headline: Anabolic Steroid Use Grows, Legal or Not
nytimes_articles.abstract: Anabolic steroid use among athletes is growing; black market is huge: an estimated 500,000 Americans, mostly young, white and male, spend total of $400 million a year on the synthetic steroid hormones; quiet revolution is under way in much smaller but booming legal market for the drug; IMS America, company that compiles data for health care industry, estimates that $36.7 million worth of anabolic steroids were sold through prescriptions or administered in hospitals last year; IMS America calculates that in first five months of 1996, sales have swelled by 38.5 percent compared with corresponding period last year (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Prayer and Politics Mingle In Dole's Visit to Olympics
nytimes_articles.abstract: Bob Dole visits site of bombing at Centennial Olympic Park, accompanied by Matt Ghaffari, American who won silver medal in Greco-Roman wrestling; Dole then heads to Olympic stadium, which has become latest stop on Presidential campaign trail; Pres Clinton has visited Games twice; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Track Queen Can Accept Bronze Age
nytimes_articles.abstract: George Vecsey's Sports of The Times column praises Olympic gold medalist Jackie Joyner-Kersee, who won bronze medal in long jump behind Chioma Ajunwa of Nigeria and Fiona May, a Briton who competes for Italy; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Tantalizing Piece of 747's Cockpit Is Found
nytimes_articles.abstract: Investigators searing watery crash site of Trans World Airlines Flight 800 discover tantalizing piece of wreckage--a section of the cockpit that they hope will lead them to other significant debris, as well as to explanation for why jumbo jet exploded in mid-air last month; piece of the cockpit, described as front-window section, was found by camera-equipped robot nosing about Boeing 747 wreckage strewn across Atlantic Ocean floor some 12 miles off the coast of eastern Long Island; map; photos (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: Corrections
U.S. Women's Team Feels Slighted by TV
nytimes_articles.abstract: US women's soccer team defeated China, 2-1, to win gold medal at Olympic Games on Aug 1, but it was nearly shut off out of prime-time television attention by NBC; and it did not please soccer team to know that the American Dream Team in men's basketball took precedence (M)D

nytimes_articles.headline: Brutal Case Illustrates Trend Of Guns' Replacing Toys
nytimes_articles.abstract: Gang rape of 13-year-old girl and killing of elderly woman in Watts section of Los Angeles draws particular attention because of age of alleged shooter--12--the brutality of the crime and the Los Angeles Police Chief's decision to make boy's name public in hope of getting him to surrender; boy was brought in by his mother; six boys and two adults were arrested earlier, but 12-year-old is thought to have pulled trigger on gun that killed Viola McClain, 82; police describe boy as 'fully street-wise 12-year-old' with prior police record; they say his mother backed down from forcing him to see his probation officer days ago when she realized he was armed; photos (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Johnson Smashes World Record and Completes Double
Medicare Ad Angers Zimmer
nytimes_articles.abstract: US Repr Richard A Zimmer has threatened to sue 10 radio stations for libel if they continue broadcasting an advertisement that accuses him of having voted to 'cut Medicare spending'; Zimmer maintains that he voted to limit growth in Medicare spending, not to cut existing benefits; some stations have agreed to stop broadcasting the ad, sponsored by advocacy group called New Jersey Citizen Action (New Jersey Daily Briefing) (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: At F.B.I. Lab, a Scientific Mission and a Challenge of Its Methods
nytimes_articles.abstract: Scientific examination of mangled pieces of wreckage from TWA Flight 800 inches forward in laboratories at FBI's J Edgar Hoover Building, Washington, DC; forensic experts mood is tense, particularly since scientists know that Justice Department, and people around the world, are looking to them to make the call on whether plane was brought down by a bomb (L)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Excerpts from interview with Pres Clinton on the economy (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: U.S. SURGICAL BEGINS A TAKEOVER BID FOR CIRCON
nytimes_articles.abstract: US Surgical Corp begins unsolicited takeover bid for smaller rival, the Circon Corp, valued at $18 a share, or about $230 million (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Youngster Escapes Mother's Lethal Grip
nytimes_articles.abstract: Police in Detroit, Mich, are drawn to Detroit River by boy claiming his mother was trying to drag him into water; they discover boy's 5-year-old brother, who dies on shore, and mother, who dies in hospital (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Officer Admits Paying to Try to Have Dallas Football Star Killed
nytimes_articles.abstract: Former Dallas police officer Johnnie Hernandez admits in court that he paid undercover narcotics agent $2,960 to have Dallas Cowboy star Michael Irvin killed; also says he sold police records to person he believed to be drug dealer; Hernandez is sentenced to six years in prison in plea agreement; Irvin has pleaded no contest to cocaine possession (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: CONTRACT AS OLYMPIC SPONSOR THROUGH 2008 REACHED
nytimes_articles.abstract: Coca-Cola Co, largest and most visible corporate sponsor of Olympics, signs agreement insuring its products will be only officially sponsored soft drinks at games through 2008; new agreement with International Olympic Committee, covers Summer Games in 2004 and 2008 and Winter Games in 2002 and 2006 (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: NEW POWER MACINTOSH LINE OF COMPUTERS IS DISPLAYED
nytimes_articles.abstract: Apple Computer Inc displays a Power Macintosh line of computers based on Power PC 604e chip; line offers speeds of as much as 200 megahertz and all models now include 8X-speed CD-ROM drives; line includes Apple's first multiprocessing desktop model, which features dual Power PC 604e processors running at 180 MHz to improve performance on computer-intensive tasks (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Lofton and Belle Help Indians Pound Orioles
nytimes_articles.abstract: Roundup of results of recent major league baseball games (L)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Bridge column describes play at quarterfinals of Grand National Teams in Miami Beach, Fla; diagrammed deal (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: How Members of Congress Voted on Minimum Wage Bill
nytimes_articles.abstract: House roll-call on bill to increase minimum wage, which passed, 354-72 (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Subway Grate Falls on Track, Causing Fire And Shutdown
nytimes_articles.abstract: Rusted Depression-era underground grate suspended high above East River subway tunnel tumbles to tracks in early morning hours, leading to electrical explosions and fire that hampers subway service to much of Queens and Manhattan for nine hours and traps dozens of riders in blinding smoke; diagram; photo (L)a

nytimes_articles.headline: Nigerian Leaps From Obscurity To Gold Medal
nytimes_articles.abstract: Chioma Ajunwa of Nigeria wins Olympic gold medal in women's long jump, with leap of 23 feet 4 1/2 inches; Fiona May of Italy wins silver with jump of 23-0 1/2; Jackie Joyner-Kersee of US wins bronze with leap of 22-11 3/4; photo (L)

nytimes_articles.headline: 10 Events, 6 Golds and a Lot of Tales

nytimes_articles.abstract: George Vecsey Sports of The Times column contends that closing ceremony of 1996 Olympic Games was tasteful homage to victims of Centennial Olympic Park bombing and also of Munich in 1972; maintains that in this day and age, putting on Summer Games may be impossible task for any host, without turning place into logistical nightmare; says he left Los Angeles, Seoul and Barcelona with magic feelings about their Summer Games, but he did not have those feelings about Atlanta's Games (M)
